12 Entry Points

Housing

1. Social Housing Allocation

Council housing waiting lists (1.2M+ households), allocation algorithms, homelessness duty, Housing Act 1996 compliance. Band-based allocation, transfer management, succession rights, and nomination agreements with registered providers across 317 English local authorities.

Planning

2. Planning Permission & Development

Planning application processing (400K+/year), local plan development, permitted development rights, enforcement. Major/minor application classification, committee decision support, Section 106 agreements, CIL charging, and planning appeal case management.

Safety

3. Building Safety & Remediation

Building Safety Act 2022 implementation, cladding remediation programme (£5.1bn), Building Safety Regulator, higher-risk building gateway process. Fire safety compliance, remediation tracking, developer contribution agreements, and leaseholder protection.

Finance

4. Local Government Finance

Council tax administration, business rates retention, Revenue Support Grant, levelling up fund allocation. Financial resilience monitoring, intervention powers, capital programme oversight, and audit compliance across 317 councils and 10 combined authorities.

Community

5. Community Empowerment

Neighbourhood planning, community right to bid, asset transfer, participatory budgeting. Community Organisers programme, parish council support, and hyper-local democratic engagement infrastructure.

Devolution

6. Devolution & Combined Authorities

10 combined authorities with elected metro mayors, devolution deals, trailblazer powers, investment funds. Mayoral combined authority governance, transport integration, skills devolution, and further devolution pipeline.

Levelling Up

7. Levelling Up Missions

12 levelling up missions — living standards, R&D, transport, broadband, education, pride in place, homeownership, wellbeing, local leadership, crime, devolution. Mission tracking dashboards, fund allocation (UKSPF, Levelling Up Fund, Towns Fund).

Regeneration

8. Urban Regeneration & Land

Brownfield land registers, Housing Infrastructure Fund, garden communities, new towns. Land assembly, compulsory purchase, remediation, and development corporation oversight for major regeneration sites.

Homelessness

9. Homelessness Prevention

Rough sleeping strategy, Housing First pilots, prevention duty, relief duty, main duty. Duty to refer, accommodation procurement, support needs assessment, and vulnerability tracking for 300K+ households in temporary accommodation.

Digital

10. Digital Planning & Data

Planning data strategy, open-source planning registers, digital site notices, BIM integration. PropTech innovation, geospatial planning data, and Local Digital Declaration compliance across planning authorities.

Regulation

11. Regulatory Oversight

Intervention powers (Secretary of State), best value inspections, commissioners, statutory directions. Corporate governance standards, officer delegation schemes, and standards committee oversight.

Accountability

12. Parliamentary Accountability

Levelling Up Select Committee, Written Questions, Statutory Instruments, NAO audits. Legislative programme (Levelling Up & Regeneration Act), ministerial accountability, and Freedom of Information obligations.

8 Transformation Priorities

Priority 1

Planning Digital Transformation

Application processing 8wk→3wk, decision accuracy +40%. AI-assisted planning application validation, constraint checking, committee report generation, and neighbour notification. Target: 80% automated validation for minor applications by 2027.

Priority 2

Social Housing Smart Allocation

Wait time 2.1yr→8mo, match quality +55%. AI-optimised allocation matching medical need, household size, employment proximity, and school catchment. Target: 90% tenant satisfaction with allocation fairness.

Priority 3

Building Safety Risk Scoring

Building assessment 18mo→4mo, risk prioritisation accuracy >90%. Automated EWS1 form analysis, cladding type identification, structural risk modelling, and remediation pathway recommendation. Target: all 11,000+ high-risk buildings scored by 2027.

Priority 4

Council Tax Fraud Detection

Fraud detection rate 12%→45%, appeals resolution 6mo→8wk. AI single-person discount verification, empty property detection, and banding accuracy audit. Target: £500M+ annual fraud prevention.

Priority 5

Homelessness Early Warning

Prevention success rate 54%→78%, rough sleeping -40%. Predictive model of eviction risk from tenancy deposit claims, rent arrears patterns, and benefit changes. Target: every at-risk household contacted before eviction.

Priority 6

Devolution Performance Dashboard

Reporting lag 12mo→real-time, fund utilisation +30%. Unified dashboard across 10 combined authorities tracking investment, jobs, transport, and skills outcomes. Target: automated GMPP-equivalent for all devolved areas.

Priority 7

Planning Enforcement Intelligence

Unauthorised development detection 20%→75%, enforcement action 6mo→6wk. Satellite change detection, planning constraint overlay, and automated enforcement notice generation. Target: continuous monitoring of all Green Belt and AONB sites.

Priority 8

Local Government Financial Resilience

Distress prediction 18mo lead time, intervention accuracy >85%. Financial ratio monitoring, Section 114 risk scoring, capital programme tracking, and statutory officer alerts. Target: zero surprise Section 114 notices.

⛔ 6 Sovereign Red Lines

  • 🚫 No housing allocation decision made solely by algorithm — human housing officer sign-off required for every allocation.
  • 🚫 No planning permission granted or refused by automated system — committee or delegated officer decision mandatory.
  • 🚫 No building safety assessment automated without Building Safety Regulator validation gateway.
  • 🚫 No council tax liability determined by AI without statutory review rights and human appeal pathway.
  • 🚫 No homelessness duty discharged by automated system — human assessment of vulnerability and priority need required.
  • 🚫 No intervention in local authority governance without Secretary of State explicit approval and statutory process.

5-Step Engagement Model

1
Discovery
Map DLUHC estate — 317 councils, 10 combined authorities, planning system, housing registers, building safety database. Identify AI-ready processes and sovereignty constraints across housing, planning, and local government pillars.
2
Governance Design
Deploy DORADO patterns — statutory decision guardrails, allocation fairness gates, planning law compliance checks. Align with Article 50, Levelling Up & Regeneration Act, and Building Safety Act 2022.
3
Pilot
Launch controlled pilots in planning validation, housing allocation matching, and building safety risk scoring. Measure against KPIs: application processing time, allocation fairness, risk detection accuracy.
4
Scale
Roll out proven MCPs across all 317 authorities. Integrate with planning portals, housing management systems, LGA platforms. Deploy sovereign OWEM adapters for planning and housing domain specialisation.
5
Assure
Continuous sovereignty verification — statutory decision compliance, red line enforcement, parliamentary accountability. NAO audit trails, Select Committee reporting, and ombudsman integration.
